subject: Last spots — dartRverse Population Genetics in R Workshop

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Last spots — dartRverse Population Genetics in R Workshop
parts:
Hi all,

We’ve got a few places left for our hands-on workshop: Population genetics in R with the dartRverse — led by the 2025 Eureka Prize–winning dartR team.

Why join?
Genomic data is everywhere, but analysis can be daunting. The dartRverse streamlines SNP and presence/absence workflows in R with an intuitive, genlight-based approach—no advanced coding required.

Who it’s for:
Ecologists, conservation biologists, and early-career researchers (R beginners welcome).

What you’ll learn (practice-first):

  • Data import and tidy workflows

  • QC & filtering for SNP/PA data

  • Diversity metrics, relatedness, F_ST, population structure

  • Reproducible analysis & visualisation

  • Tips for reporting and sharing results

When & where:
📍 Canberra
🗓️ 12–14 Nov 2025
⏰ 9:00–17:00 daily

Register:
https://cba.anu.edu.au/news-events/events/snp-happens-explore-population-genetics-dartrverse

Spots are limited—grab yours soon.

On behalf of the dartR team, hope to see you there!

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Last spots — dartRverse Population Genetics in R Workshop
parts:
Dear dartR team,
Thank you for organizing the upcoming workshop on population genetics in R with the dartRverse. I am very eager to participate, as the content aligns closely with my research interests and ongoing work in rice genetics and conservation in West Africa.
However, I am currently facing financial constraints and, as a researcher based in Mali, a low-income country, I would be sincerely grateful if you could consider granting me a fee waiver or allowing me to attend free of charge.
This opportunity would greatly enhance my capacity to apply reproducible genomic workflows in my region, and I am committed to sharing the knowledge gained with local students and collaborators.
Thank you very much for your kind consideration. I look forward to your response.
